To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
eddy current loss is affected by the thickness of the copper strip and that shielding of the perpendicular magnetic field is possible with a thin copper strip.
shielding of perpendicular magnetic field by metal strips in high-temperature superconductor coated conductors is complete and that the loss is independent of the metal strip thickness.
the eddy current losses in metal layers of REBCO superconducting tapes and Roebel cables can be reduced by stacking the samples vertically with a perpendicular applied magnetic field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the eddy current shielding effect by metal strips in the REBCO superconducting tapes and the Roebel cables.
the shielding of perpendicular fields in the metal layer of REBCO superconducting tapes.
the shielding of perpendicular ac magnetic fields in the metal layers of REBCO superconducting tapes and Roebel cables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no eddy current loss at low field amplitude and there is a small amount of eddy current loss even at high field amplitude.
shielding of perpendicular magnetic field in the copper layer of the REBCO superconductor can be achieved by the superconductivity of the REBCOs.
the perpendicular shielding is complete at low magnetic field amplitudes and the loss is independent of the copper strip thickness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shielding of perpendicular fields by the copper strips stacked with the Fujikura tapes and the Roebel cable is effective even at high field amplitude.
the shielding of perpendicular fields by the stabilizing metal layer is effective in the low magnetic field amplitude range and is independent of the stabilizing layer thickness.
eddy current loss is strongly affected by the superconductor and the superconductor can shield the perpendicular magnetic fields in metal layers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the shielding of perpendicular fields in metal-stabilized layers of REBCO superconducting tapes and Roebel cables is effective at low applied magnetic field amplitude and is not affected by the metal layer thickness up to 1 mm.
the eddy current losses in metal layers in high-temperature superconductor tapes can be estimated by measuring the ac loss of a stack with the metal layer and a tape without the metal layer.
the shielding of perpendicular fields is not affected by the width of the copper strips or the width of the superconducting layers, and that the shielding is not degraded by stacking multiple layers.
